hero.lead: A mountain nation of 3.1 million in the South Caucasus, growing 5.5% in 2026 on IMF projections, which borrows from the World Bank for health and energy and raised its own contribution to the Bank’s fund for the poorest nations by 30% in 2025.

capital.heading: A borrower that also gives: health, energy and investment.

register.name: Eurobond due 2035
register.detail: Republic of Armenia · coupon 6.750% · yield 7.100% · priced 5 March 2025 · matures 12 March 2035
register.note: Settled on 12 March 2025; net proceeds for general governmental purposes
register.text: A ten-year US dollar bond of the Republic of Armenia sold to international investors, priced on 5 March 2025 with a coupon of 6.750% and a yield of 7.100%. Its net proceeds go to general governmental purposes, the public finances behind all seven standards.

register.name: Economic Transformation Development Policy Operation
register.detail: World Bank · P508569 · approved 30 March 2026 · EUR 170.3 million
register.note: The OPEC Fund intends to provide parallel financing of up to $92.8 million, for a package of about $290 million
register.text: Budget support approved on 30 March 2026 for reforms that modernise the investment climate, strengthen competition and consumer protection, and build resilience into fiscal and regulatory systems, including a new Climate Law and a green taxonomy. It finances the public budget behind all seven standards and serves the livelihood standard through investment and trade.

register.name: Housing Response and Mortgage Market Enhancement Project
register.detail: World Bank · P508310 · approved 23 December 2025 · includes a $24.4 million GCFF grant and a $10 million Livable Planet Fund grant
register.note: Rental assistance for over 40,000 refugees; about 6,500 refugee households helped to buy permanent homes
register.text: Financing for the government’s Refugees Housing Support State Program: immediate rental assistance for more than 40,000 refugees and mortgage subsidies to help about 6,500 refugee households acquire permanent homes. It also supports the National Mortgage Company in refinancing banks that lend under the programme, and serves the shelter standard.

register.name: Stand-By Arrangement (precautionary)
register.detail: IMF · 36 months · approved December 2025 · 100% of quota · about US$175 million
register.note: SDR 18.4 million (about US$25 million) available on approval; the authorities intend to treat it as precautionary
register.text: A 36-month arrangement approved by the IMF Executive Board, announced on 3 December 2025, as the Board completed the sixth review of the previous arrangement and cancelled it. The authorities intend to treat it as precautionary: a reserve behind the macroeconomic stability on which spending for the seven standards depends.

register.name: Water and Irrigation Services Enhancement Program
register.detail: World Bank · June 2025 · the programme mobilises $435 million in total, including $330 million from IBRD
register.note: In the World Bank’s current portfolio for Armenia
register.text: A World Bank loan of June 2025 for drinking water supply and irrigation services; the World Bank states that the programme will mobilise $435 million in total, including $330 million from IBRD. It serves the water standard and, through irrigation, the food standard.

register.name: Tourism and Regional Infrastructure Project
register.detail: World Bank · press release of 17 April 2025
register.note: Listed at $100.2 million in the World Bank’s current portfolio for Armenia
register.text: A World Bank loan for local tourism infrastructure in the regions, to create jobs and attract private investment. It serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Enabling Universal Health Coverage Program
register.detail: World Bank · P179482 · Program for Results · approved 28 June 2024
register.note: In the World Bank’s current portfolio for Armenia
register.text: A results-based World Bank loan to bring universal health coverage within reach in Armenia. It serves the health standard.

register.name: Enabling the Energy Transition Program
register.detail: World Bank · P179336 · Program for Results · approved 30 May 2024
register.note: In the World Bank’s current portfolio for Armenia
register.text: A results-based World Bank loan that supports Armenia’s shift to clean power. It serves the energy standard.

register.name: Second Green, Resilient and Inclusive Development Policy Operation
register.detail: World Bank · P179849 · approved 24 April 2024
register.note: Budget support
register.text: World Bank budget support for green, resilient and inclusive reforms. It finances the public budget behind the seven standards.

register.name: Seismic Safety Improvement Program 3
register.detail: ADB · loan agreement signed with the Government of Armenia · 17 July 2026 · third ADB loan to the programme
register.note: An additional 50 schools to be rebuilt; 46 supported to date
register.text: The third ADB loan for Armenia’s Seismic Safety Improvement Program, after $88.5 million in 2015 and $72.3 million in 2023, to expand resilient, inclusive school infrastructure and strengthen the capacity to manage earthquake risks. It will enable the reconstruction of 50 more schools across the country, and serves the education standard.

register.name: Resilience and Growth Plan for Armenia
register.detail: European Union · announced April 2024 · financing agreement for 2025–2027 signed 19 March 2026
register.note: The financing agreement allows the remaining funds under the Plan to be implemented
register.text: The European Union’s €270 million Resilience and Growth Plan in support of Armenia, announced in April 2024 by the President of the European Commission. The financing agreement for 2025–2027, signed at a meeting in Yerevan on 19 March 2026, allows the remaining funds under the Plan to be implemented, in support of the economy and livelihoods behind the seven standards.

register.name: Fiscal Sustainability and Financial Markets Development Program, subprogram 3
register.detail: ADB · policy-based loan · approved 10 March 2026 · 15 years, including a grace period of 3 years
register.note: Budget support from ADB’s ordinary capital resources, the third subprogram of the programme
register.text: A policy-based ADB loan for the third subprogram of the Fiscal Sustainability and Financial Markets Development Program, approved by the ADB Board on 10 March 2026. It finances the state budget behind all seven standards and supports the development of Armenia’s financial markets.

register.name: Transformative Housing Reforms for Improved Vitality and Empowerment Program
register.detail: ADB · results-based loan · committed in 2025 · with a $16.45 million GCFF grant
register.note: Housing for about 109,000 ethnic Armenian refugees
register.text: A results-based ADB loan, with a $16.45 million grant from the Global Concessional Financing Facility, committed in 2025 for the housing needs of about 109,000 ethnic Armenian refugees. It serves the shelter standard, alongside the World Bank’s housing project for refugees.

register.name: Loan to the Central Bank of Armenia for small businesses
register.detail: EIB Global · press release of 29 October 2025 · backed by EFSD+
register.note: Around 500 enterprises and about 14,000 jobs; at least 45% outside Yerevan
register.text: An EIB Global loan to the Central Bank of Armenia, passed on through commercial banks and universal credit organisations to micro, small and medium-sized enterprises and mid-caps. At least 45% goes to businesses outside Yerevan, at least 30% to enterprises promoting gender equality and at least 40% to green projects; it serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Socio-economic development in Syunik province
register.detail: EIB Global · loan to the Republic of Armenia · 17 July 2025 · Resilient Syunik Team Europe Initiative
register.note: Safe drinking water for over 30,000 people across Syunik
register.text: An EIB Global loan to the Republic of Armenia for reliable drinking water, education and health services in Syunik, the southernmost province, including upgraded polyclinics and vocational centres. The EU states it will bring safe drinking water to over 30,000 people; it serves the water, health and education standards.

register.name: Health Care Quality Improvement Program
register.detail: ADB · results-based loan · approved 7 November 2024 · $50 million equivalent · $2 million grant from the Japan Fund for Prosperous and Resilient Asia and the Pacific
register.note: 24 health facilities to be built or rehabilitated
register.text: A results-based ADB loan for the construction or rehabilitation of 24 health facilities designed to be climate- and gender-responsive, with stronger quality of care, digital health and the health workforce. It serves the health standard.

register.name: Caucasus Transmission Network
register.detail: KfW loan €120 million with German Federal Government risk cover · EU grant €15 million · signed 19 March 2026
register.note: Total support to the project reaches €313.2 million; the EIB co-finances
register.text: Financing agreements signed on 19 March 2026 for the Caucasus Transmission Network: a €120 million KfW loan and a €15 million grant from the EU Neighbourhood Investment Platform. The project strengthens Armenia’s energy security, expands renewable generation and connects Armenia’s power market to its region; it serves the energy standard.

register.name: Loan to Converse Bank for women-owned MSMEs and sustainable lending
register.detail: ADB · up to $13 million ADB loan and $2 million from CANPA · 26 June 2026
register.note: At least 20% of the on-lending to women-owned enterprises
register.text: An ADB loan of up to $13 million and a $2 million ADB-administered loan from the Canadian Climate and Nature Fund for the Private Sector in Asia. Of the ADB loan, $11 million will be on-lent to micro, small and medium-sized enterprises, at least 20% of it to women-owned firms, and $2 million supports sustainable MSME and household lending; it serves the livelihood standard.
by: Canadian Climate and Nature Fund for the Private Sector in Asia

register.name: Loans to ArmSwissBank for refugee-owned and youth-led businesses
register.detail: EBRD · two loans of US$10 million each · signed at the EBRD 2026 Annual Meeting in Riga · EU first-loss cover through EFSD+
register.note: Eligible borrowers can access EU-funded investment grants of up to 35% of their loan
register.text: Two EBRD loans to ArmSwissBank: one under the EU4Business-EBRD Credit Line for refugee-owned and refugee-led firms and businesses that employ displaced people, and one under the Youth in Business programme for young entrepreneurs. The EU adds grants, advisory support and first-loss risk cover; it serves the livelihood standard for refugees and young people.

register.name: Loan to Ameriabank for MSMEs and green finance
register.detail: ADB · loan agreement signed May 2026 · up to 75% for MSME lending, at least 25% for green finance
register.note: At least 10% for women-owned MSMEs
register.text: An ADB loan of up to $100 million to Ameriabank to expand lending to micro, small and medium-sized enterprises and to finance renewable energy and energy efficiency, with at least 10% for women-owned MSMEs. It serves the livelihood and energy standards.

register.name: EU-backed guarantee for new small-business loans by Ameriabank
register.detail: EIB Group · EU4Business Guarantee Facility · 8 May 2026 · new loans of up to €106.25 million
register.note: About 900 MSMEs and over 5,000 jobs expected; the amount of the guarantee itself is not disclosed
register.text: A partial portfolio guarantee from the EIB Group that enables Ameriabank to build a portfolio of new loans of up to €106.25 million to micro, small and medium-sized enterprises, made possible by the EU4Business Guarantee Facility. It serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Loan to Ardshinbank for small businesses
register.detail: EIB Global · signed 12 December 2025 in Yerevan · about 10% for green lending
register.note: Around 300 Armenian firms and more than 10,000 jobs expected
register.text: An EIB Global loan to Ardshinbank for micro, small and medium-sized enterprises and mid-caps, partly in local currency and with EU grant funding for affordability. About 10% is earmarked for green lending such as energy efficiency and renewable energy; it serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Loan to Ameriabank for small businesses
register.detail: EIB Global · press release of 3 February 2025 · at least 20% for green investment
register.note: Around 400 small businesses and over 15,000 jobs; EIB Global’s largest direct loan to a bank in the South Caucasus
register.text: A direct EIB Global loan to Ameriabank for investments by micro, small and medium-sized enterprises and mid-caps, partly in local currency and with EU grant funding to keep the interest rate affordable. At least 20% goes to green investments; it serves the livelihood standard.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Minerals
items.label: Of GDP from mineral rents, 2021
items.text: Copper and molybdenum mines that already earn: value to keep at home.

items.name: The Clean Grid
items.label: Of electricity from renewable sources, 2021
items.text: Three tenths of the power from water and sun, with room for much more.

items.name: The Diaspora
items.label: Of GDP sent home by citizens abroad, 2025
items.text: Armenians abroad send home a steady share of the economy.

items.name: The Farmland
items.label: Of the land in agriculture, 2023
items.text: Land that can feed the nation and earn abroad, valued and financed against its harvest.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 19% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.

items.name: Fuller Center for Housing Armenia
items.text: A non-profit that builds and renovates homes for low-income families and provides them with long-term, interest-free housing loans, whose repayments go into a revolving fund that helps more families. Its spring 2024 newsletter reports that 309 families have received assistance over 14 years through its partnership with the ICRC.

items.name: SkyAgro
items.text: An Armenian startup that uses drones to make crop spraying more efficient, particularly for small farms, which the source reports lets farmers use 30% to 40% less chemicals and water. It serves around 700 farmers in Armenia.

items.name: Teach For Armenia
items.text: An educational foundation that recruits young leaders from Armenia and the diaspora to teach for two years in schools where their skills are needed. In July 2024 it signed a World Bank grant of up to US$2.6 million for a project on mental health and psychosocial support in Armenian schools.

items.name: Homeland Development Initiative Foundation (HDIF)
items.text: A Yerevan non-profit founded in 2013 that creates paid work for women in rural and border communities, whose handicrafts it designs, markets and sells, including to diplomatic missions, international organisations and businesses. Its producer partners work in Talin, Gyumri, Koghb, Berd, Vardenis, Vayk and Goghovit, and its Arm.wool project revives Armenia’s wool heritage.
